abu-dhabi-university.name: Abu Dhabi University
abu-dhabi-university.brief: Abu Dhabi University is a private research university in the United Arab Emirates. Its main campus is in Khalifa City, Abu Dhabi, with satellite campuses in Al Ain, Dubai and Madinat Zayed. It was founded in 2003 by Ali Saeed bin Harmal al-Dhaheri. Main areas of study include arts, education, social sciences, business, engineering, health sciences and law. Programmes run from undergraduate to postgraduate level. The university is organised into five colleges.

aston-university.name: Aston University
aston-university.brief: Aston University is a public university in the city centre of Birmingham, England. It was founded in 1895 as the Birmingham Municipal Technical School, and became the UK's first college of advanced technology in 1956. Main subject areas include business, law, medicine, engineering and physical sciences, and computer science. Study locations are Birmingham, London and Online. Academic schools include Aston Business School, Aston Law School and Aston Medical School.

brunel-university-of-london.name: Brunel University London
brunel-university-of-london.brief: Brunel University London is a public research university in Uxbridge, west London, England. It is named after Isambard Kingdom Brunel, a Victorian engineer. The university describes itself as one of the UK's foremost technical universities, with research and teaching in business, health, tech and engineering. Brunel is a single-site campus at Kingston Lane, Uxbridge.

chalmers-university-of-technology.name: Chalmers University of Technology
chalmers-university-of-technology.brief: Chalmers University of Technology is a university in Gothenburg, Sweden. It conducts research and education in technology, natural sciences, maritime studies and architecture. Its postal address is Chalmers tekniska högskola, 412 96 Göteborg. Master's programmes are offered, including New Space Systems Engineering.

curtin-university.name: Curtin University
curtin-university.brief: Curtin University is an Australian public research university based in Bentley, Perth, Western Australia. It is named after John Curtin, Prime Minister of Australia from 1941 to 1945. Main areas of study include agriculture, environment and sustainability; architecture and construction; arts and creative industries; business, innovation, management and law; education; engineering, mining and surveying; health; information technology; and physical sciences, geoscience and mathematics. Its largest campus is Curtin Perth, and the university also has campuses in Kalgoorlie, Midland, Malaysia, Singapore, Dubai, Mauritius and Colombo.

duke-university.name: Duke University
duke-university.brief: Duke University is a private research university in Durham, North Carolina, United States. It was founded by Methodists and Quakers in the present-day city of Trinity in 1838, and the school moved to Durham in 1892. Its schools include the Divinity School, Fuqua School of Business, Nicholas School of the Environment, Pratt School of Engineering, Sanford School of Public Policy, School of Law, School of Medicine, School of Nursing, and Trinity College of Arts & Sciences. Duke also runs Duke Kunshan University and Duke-NUS Medical School.

erasmus-university-rotterdam.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
erasmus-university-rotterdam.brief: Erasmus University Rotterdam is a public research university in Rotterdam, Netherlands, named after Desiderius Erasmus Roterodamus, a 15th-century Christian humanist and theologian. Its campuses are on four locations, three in Rotterdam and one in The Hague. Study areas include bachelor and master programmes, and the university lists Erasmus School of Economics among its units.

georgia-institute-of-technology.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
georgia-institute-of-technology.brief: Georgia Institute of Technology is a public research university and institute of technology in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. Satellite campuses are in Savannah, Georgia, and Metz, France. Its colleges include Computing, Design, Engineering, Lifetime Learning, Sciences, Liberal Arts, and Business. Its Atlanta campus sits in Midtown.

maastricht-university.brief: Maastricht University is a public research university in Maastricht, Netherlands. Founded in 1976, it is the second youngest of the fourteen Dutch universities. The library has about 3000 study places in seven different locations across Maastricht city. Its pages describe Problem-Based Learning and programmes in Arts and Social Sciences, Business and Economics, Health, Medicine and Life Sciences, Law, Psychology and Neuroscience, and Science and Engineering. Its campuses include University College Maastricht, University College Venlo and Maastricht Science Programme, and it has offices in Venlo and Heerlen.

michigan-state-university.name: Michigan State University
michigan-state-university.brief: Michigan State University is a public land-grant research university in East Lansing, Michigan, United States. It was founded in 1855 as the Agricultural College of the State of Michigan. MSU offers more than 400 programs of study across 16 degree-granting colleges. Its campus is 5,200 acres, with 27 residence halls.

newcastle-university.name: Newcastle University
newcastle-university.brief: Newcastle University is a public research university in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. It has overseas campuses in Singapore and Malaysia. The university is organised into faculties, schools and research units. Study areas include undergraduate, postgraduate taught, postgraduate research and pathway courses.

oxford-brookes-university.name: Oxford Brookes University
oxford-brookes-university.brief: Oxford Brookes University is a public university in Oxford, England. It received university status through the Further and Higher Education Act 1992. The university says it has over 150 years of history and started out as a small School of Art. It has 12 schools within 2 faculties, covering areas such as business, law, nursing, architecture, engineering and psychology. Its campuses include Harcourt Hill, Headington and Swindon.

purdue-university.name: Purdue University
purdue-university.brief: Purdue University is a public land-grant research university in the United States. Its main campus is in West Lafayette, Indiana, and it also has an urban campus in Indianapolis. The university was founded in 1869. Its colleges and schools include agriculture, business, education, engineering, health and human sciences, liberal arts, pharmacy, science, and veterinary medicine.

rheinisch-westfalische-technische-hochsc.name: Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule Aachen
rheinisch-westfalische-technische-hochsc.brief: RWTH Aachen University (Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule) is a public research university located in Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is a technical university, one of the TU9 universities in Germany. The Research Campus and Campus Melaten and Campus West are named.

ruhr-universitat-bochum.name: Ruhr University Bochum
ruhr-universitat-bochum.brief: Ruhr University Bochum is a public research university in Bochum, Germany, in the southern hills of the central Ruhr area. It was founded in 1962 as the first new public university in Germany after World War II. Its main areas of study include a wide variety of subjects across 21 faculties. The university describes a compact campus that brings researchers together across disciplinary boundaries.

stanford-university.name: Stanford University
stanford-university.brief: Stanford University is a private research university in Stanford, California, United States. It was founded in 1885 by railroad magnate Leland Stanford and his wife, Jane. Its main areas of study include business, sustainability, education, engineering and medicine. It is organised into seven schools on one contiguous campus, and it has a Stanford Health Care unit and athletics programmes.

taylor-s-university.name: Taylor's University
taylor-s-university.brief: Taylor's University is a private university in Subang Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia, and part of Taylor's Education Group. The Group runs K-12 schools, a college and a British university campus in Vietnam, with a presence across Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam. Its group headquarters is at No.1, Jalan Taylor's, 47500 Subang Jaya, Selangor Darul Ehsan, Malaysia.

texas-a-m-university.name: Texas A&M University
texas-a-m-university.brief: Texas A&M University is a public land-grant research university in College Station, Texas, United States. It was founded in 1876 and became the flagship institution of the Texas A&M University System in 1948. Its main campus is in College Station, with additional campuses in McAllen, Fort Worth, Washington, D.C., Galveston, and Qatar. It has 17 colleges and schools on the main College Station campus, covering areas such as agriculture, engineering, business, medicine, law, and veterinary medicine.

umea-university.brief: Umeå University is a public research university in Umeå, in the mid-northern region of Sweden. It was founded in 1965 and is one of Sweden's larger comprehensive universities. Its work covers education and research across many fields, including medicine, science and technology, social sciences, arts and humanities, and education. The university has four faculties and seven schools and institutes, and most teaching and research takes place in departments and sections. It runs a Healthy Campus programme and works with the EC2U alliance of European universities.

universiti-teknologi-petronas.brief: Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP) is a private research university in Malaysia. It is located in Seri Iskandar, Perak. Its areas of study include engineering, applied science, management, computing, geoscience and petroleum engineering. It has two faculties, the Faculty of Engineering and the Faculty of Science, Management & Computing, plus the Centre for Foundation Studies. Its campus spans 400 hectares.

university-of-bergen.brief: The University of Bergen (UiB) is a public research university in Bergen, Norway. It describes itself as an internationally recognised research university, with research communities across the full breadth of academic disciplines. The university offers research-based study programmes. Its units are organised into faculties and departments. Its research collaborations and clusters include the Media Cluster Norway and the Trond Mohn Research Foundation.

university-of-california-berkeley.name: University of California, Berkeley
university-of-california-berkeley.brief: The University of California, Berkeley is a public land-grant research university in Berkeley, California, United States. It was founded in 1868 and is the state's first land-grant university and the founding campus of the University of California system. Its areas of study include business, engineering, law, public health, journalism, education and natural resources. The university has 15 schools and colleges, among them the College of Letters & Science, the largest college.

university-of-california-santa-barbara.name: University of California, Santa Barbara
university-of-california-santa-barbara.brief: University of California, Santa Barbara is a public land-grant research university in Santa Barbara County, California, United States. It traces its roots to 1891 as an independent teachers college and joined the University of California system in 1944. Main areas of study include letters and science, engineering, creative studies, environmental science and management, and education.

university-of-colorado-boulder.name: University of Colorado Boulder
university-of-colorado-boulder.brief: University of Colorado Boulder is a public research university in Boulder, Colorado, United States. It was founded in 1876, five months before Colorado became a state, and is the flagship university of the University of Colorado system. Main areas include the natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, business, education, engineering and applied science, law, music, and communication, media, design and information. The university is organised into colleges and schools, including the College of Arts and Sciences, Leeds School of Business, and College of Engineering & Applied Science.

university-of-florida.name: University of Florida
university-of-florida.brief: The University of Florida is a public land-grant research university in Gainesville, Florida, United States. It is a senior member of the State University System of Florida. The university offers more than 300 degree options from 16 academic colleges, including agriculture, arts, business, engineering, law, medicine and veterinary medicine. Its main campus is in Gainesville, and it also has UF Health facilities in Gainesville, Jacksonville and Orlando. The university is organised into 16 colleges across its Gainesville campus.

universitat-hamburg.brief: The University of Hamburg is a public research university in Hamburg, Germany. It was founded on 28 March 1919 by combining the previous General Lecture System, the Hamburg Colonial Institute, and the Academic College. Its main areas of study include law, business, economics and social sciences, medicine, education, humanities, mathematics, informatics and natural sciences, and psychology and human movement science.

lancaster-university.name: University of Lancaster
lancaster-university.brief: Lancaster University is a collegiate public research university in Lancaster, Lancashire, England. It was established in 1964 by royal charter. Its main areas of study include health and medicine, humanities, arts and social sciences, management, and science and technology. Its main campus is at Bailrigg, and it has four academic faculties, each with its own departments and schools.

universitat-mannheim.name: University of Mannheim
universitat-mannheim.brief: The University of Mannheim is a public research university in Mannheim, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It was founded in 1967. Its main areas of study include Business Administration, Economics, Law, Business Informatics, Mathematics, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, Linguistics, History, and Media and Communication Studies. The university is organised into schools and departments: the Department of Law, the Department of Economics, the Business School, the School of Social Sciences, the School of Humanities, and the School of Business Informatics and Mathematics.

university-of-minnesota.name: University of Minnesota
university-of-minnesota.brief: The University of Minnesota Twin Cities is a public land-grant research university in the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, Minnesota, United States. It is the flagship institution of the University of Minnesota System. The university offers 300+ undergraduate majors & minors. It is organized into 19 colleges, schools, and other major academic units. Its campuses include Crookston, Duluth, Morris, Rochester, and Twin Cities.

university-of-notre-dame.name: University of Notre Dame
university-of-notre-dame.brief: The University of Notre Dame is a private Catholic research university in Notre Dame, Indiana, United States. It was founded in 1842 by members of the Congregation of Holy Cross, a Catholic religious order of priests and brothers. Its main areas of study include arts and letters, business, engineering, global affairs, law, science and architecture. The university is organised into colleges and schools, including the Mendoza College of Business, the College of Engineering and the College of Science. The campus is shown on a campus map with buildings, parking and dining locations.

universite-paris-1-pantheon-sorbonne.name: University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne
universite-paris-1-pantheon-sorbonne.brief: Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University is a public research university in Paris, France. It was created in 1971 from two faculties of the historic University of Paris after the May 1968 protests. The university offers courses taught in English and summer schools in various academic fields, including economics and law. Its locations include the Centre Pierre-Mendès-France, Centre Panthéon, Centre du Four, Centre Saint-Charles, Centre Lourcine, Centre René-Cassin, Centre Sorbonne and Centre La Chapelle, all in Paris.

university-of-reading.name: University of Reading
university-of-reading.brief: The University of Reading is a public research university in Reading, Berkshire, England. It was founded in 1892 as the University Extension College, Reading, and became University College, Reading in 1902. Its areas of study include agriculture, archaeology, architecture, business, chemistry, computer science, economics, engineering, law, mathematics, medicine-related sciences, psychology and many others. The university has campuses at Whiteknights, London Road and Greenlands, and a campus in Malaysia.

university-of-southern-california.name: University of Southern California
university-of-southern-california.brief: The University of Southern California is a private research university in Los Angeles, California, United States. It was founded in 1880 by Robert M. It has a constellation of schools, centers and institutes. Main areas include Letters, Arts and Sciences, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Business, Cinematic Arts and Dentistry. The University Park Campus and the Health Sciences Campus are listed among its campuses.

university-of-surrey.name: University of Surrey
university-of-surrey.brief: The University of Surrey is a public research university in Guildford, Surrey, England. It received its royal charter in 1966, following recommendations in the Robbins Report. Its main areas include arts, business and social sciences; engineering and physical sciences; health and medical sciences; and veterinary medicine. It is organised into faculties and schools, with institutes and the Surrey Institute of Education. It also has an international branch campus at GIFT City, India.

university-of-toronto.name: University of Toronto
university-of-toronto.brief: The University of Toronto is a public research university in the Greater Toronto Area of Ontario, Canada. It was founded by royal charter in 1827 as King's College, the first institution of higher learning in Upper Canada. Its academic programs are organized into faculties and divisions, including Applied Science & Engineering, Arts & Science, Medicine, Law, Management and Music. It has three campuses: St. George (downtown Toronto), Mississauga (west of Toronto) and Scarborough (eastern Toronto).

university-of-york.name: University of York
university-of-york.brief: The University of York is a collegiate public research university in York, England. It was established in 1963 and has more than thirty departments and centres covering a wide range of subjects. It is a member of the Russell Group. Its main areas include Arts and Humanities, Sciences and Social Sciences. Campuses are East Campus and West Campus in York, with international campuses in Mumbai, India and Thessaloniki and Athens, Greece.

vanderbilt-university.name: Vanderbilt University
vanderbilt-university.brief: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, United States. It was founded in 1873. It offers more than 65 undergraduate majors and a full range of graduate and professional degrees. The university has 12 schools and colleges and a 340-acre campus in Nashville. Its planned and current campuses include New York City, West Palm Beach, San Francisco and Chattanooga.

washington-university-in-st-louis.name: Washington University in St. Louis
washington-university-in-st-louis.brief: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU) is a private research university in the St. Louis area, United States. Its main areas of study include the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences in Arts & Sciences, engineering, business, design, law, medicine and public health. The university has nine schools and a range of departments. Its two main campuses are the Danforth Campus and the Medical Campus.

adelaide-university.name: Adelaide University
adelaide-university.brief: Adelaide University is a public research university based in Adelaide, Australia. It was founded in 2024 and officially opened on 29 January 2026, after merging the University of Adelaide and the University of South Australia (UniSA). It has six colleges: College of Business and Law, College of Creative Arts, Design and Humanities, College of Education, Behavioural and Social Sciences, College of Engineering and Information Technology, College of Health, and College of Science. It has seven campuses across South Australia, including Adelaide City Campus, Magill, Mawson Lakes, Mount Gambier, Roseworthy, Waite and Whyalla.

dalhousie-university.brief: Dalhousie University is a large public research university in Nova Scotia, Canada. It offers over 200 degree programs in 13 undergraduate, graduate, and professional faculties. Its main campuses are in Halifax, with a fourth campus in Bible Hill (Truro), and satellite medical school campuses in Saint John, New Brunswick and Cape Breton. The university was founded in the year stated on its founding page, and its faculties include Agriculture, Architecture and Planning, Arts and Social Sciences, Computer Science, Dentistry, Engineering, Health, Law, Management, Medicine, and Science.

flinders-university.name: Flinders University
flinders-university.brief: Flinders University is a public research university in Adelaide, South Australia. It was founded in 1966 and named after the British navigator Matthew Flinders. Its study areas include business, computer science and information technology, creative arts and media, criminology, education, engineering, health, law, medicine, nursing and midwifery, psychology, science and social work. Its campuses include Bedford Park, Tonsley and City Campus. Its colleges include Business, Creative Arts, Law and Social Sciences; Human Sciences and Culture; Health and Enablement; and Medicine and Public Health.

goethe-universitat-frankfurt-am-main.name: Goethe University Frankfurt
goethe-universitat-frankfurt-am-main.brief: Goethe University Frankfurt is a public research university in Frankfurt am Main, Hesse, Germany. It was founded in 1914 as a citizens' university. Its main areas include the humanities and social sciences, the natural, life, and medical sciences. The university has five locations in Frankfurt: Westend, Riedberg, Niederrad, Ginnheim and Bockenheim campuses.

imperial-college-london.name: Imperial College London
imperial-college-london.brief: Imperial College London is a public research university in London, England, also known as Imperial. It works in areas including engineering, medicine, natural sciences and business. Its main faculties are the Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Medicine, Faculty of Natural Sciences and Imperial Business School. Imperial has several campuses in London and the South East, including South Kensington, White City and Silwood Park, plus hospital campuses.

johannes-gutenberg-universitat-mainz.name: Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz
johannes-gutenberg-universitat-mainz.brief: Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is a public research university in Mainz, Rhineland Palatinate, Germany. It is named after the inventor Johannes Gutenberg since 1946. Its research areas include particle physics, materials sciences, quantum and atomic physics, sustainable chemistry and polymer chemistry, life sciences and translational medicine. JGU forms the Rhine-Main Universities alliance (RMU) with Goethe University Frankfurt and the Technical University of Darmstadt.

king-s-college-london.name: King's College London
king-s-college-london.brief: King's College London is a public research university in London, England. It was established by royal charter in 1829. Its main areas of study include arts and humanities, business, dentistry, law, life sciences and medicine, natural, mathematical and engineering sciences, nursing, psychiatry, psychology and neuroscience, and social science and public policy. Its faculties include the Faculty of Arts & Humanities, the Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences and the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine.

linkoping-university.name: Linköping University
linkoping-university.brief: Linköping University is a public research university based in Linköping, Sweden. It was established in 1969 and granted full university status in 1975. The university offers study programmes in fields including medicine, health care, public health, biomedical engineering, and furniture design. It is organised across four campuses at three locations in southern Sweden: Campus Valla, Campus US, Campus Norrköping and Campus Lidingö.

macquarie-university.name: Macquarie University
macquarie-university.brief: Macquarie University is a public research university in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. It is research-intensive. Main areas of study listed include Business, Education, Engineering, Law, Science, Medicine and health, Arts and social sciences, Information technologies, Languages and linguistics, Media, communications and creative arts, Psychology and cognitive science, and Security, intelligence and criminology. Its top-level faculties include the Faculty of Arts, the Macquarie Business School, and the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences.

universite-paris-cite.brief: Université Paris Cité is a public research university located in Paris, France. It was created by decree on 20 March 2019, through the merger of Paris Descartes and Paris Diderot universities. Its main areas include Health, Sciences, and Humanities and social sciences. Its headquarters is at 85 boulevard Saint-Germain in Paris, with sites across Paris and some overseas territories. It is organised into faculties and departments, including UFRs, schools and institutes.

queen-mary-university-of-london.name: Queen Mary University of London
queen-mary-university-of-london.brief: Queen Mary University of London is a public research university in London, England, and a member institution of the federal University of London. Its history dates back to 1785, with the founding of The London Hospital Medical College. Its main areas of study include medicine, dentistry, science and engineering, humanities, social sciences, law, business and economics. It has five campuses in London, with its main campuses at Mile End and Whitechapel, and three faculties: Humanities and Social Sciences, Science and Engineering, and Medicine and Dentistry. It also has international campuses in Paris, Malta and China.

rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.name: Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn
rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.brief: The University of Bonn is a public research university in Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It was founded in its present form as the Rhein-Universität on 18 October 1818. Its main areas of study include economics, mathematics, physics, law, agriculture, theology and the arts, with around 200 subject areas. The university has seven faculties and campuses in the city centre, Poppelsdorf, Endenich, Venusberg and Klein-Altendorf.

faculties.name: Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences

ruprecht-karls-universitat-heidelberg.name: Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg
ruprecht-karls-universitat-heidelberg.brief: Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg is a public research university in Heidelberg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It was founded in 1386 on instruction of Pope Urban VI and is Germany's oldest university. The university describes itself as a comprehensive research university. It offers over 160 fields of study across a broad spectrum of subjects. Its faculties are grouped into Mathematics, Engineering Sciences, and Natural Sciences; Liberal Arts; Law, Economics, and Social Sciences; and Medicine.

faculties.name: Mathematics, Engineering Sciences, and Natural Sciences

technical-university-of-munich.name: Technical University of Munich
technical-university-of-munich.brief: The Technical University of Munich is a public research university in Munich, Bavaria, Germany. It specializes in engineering, technology, medicine, and applied and natural sciences. The university's pages describe it as The Entrepreneurial University. Its website lists Schools and Research Centers, and its pages cover degree programs for bachelor's and master's study. Information for international applicants, including application, admission and tuition fees for students from non-EU countries, is provided on the site.

tilburg-university.name: Tilburg University
tilburg-university.brief: Tilburg University is a Catholic research university in Tilburg, Netherlands. It was founded in 1927 and specializes in the social and behavioral sciences, economics, law, business sciences, theology and humanities. It has a compact, green campus with buildings such as Academia, Cobbenhagen, Dante and Koopmans. Faculties include Tilburg School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences, Tilburg School Economics and Management, and Tilburg Law School.

united-arab-emirates-university.name: United Arab Emirates University
united-arab-emirates-university.brief: United Arab Emirates University (UAEU) is a public research university located in Al Ain, United Arab Emirates. It was founded in 1976 by the country's first President, Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, and is the oldest university in the country. It offers courses in various subjects up to graduate school. Its main areas include undergraduate and graduate programs organised through colleges. Its pages also describe campus life and facilities, and its research units and centers.

the-university-of-amsterdam.name: University of Amsterdam
the-university-of-amsterdam.brief: The University of Amsterdam is a public research university located in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It was established in 1632 by municipal authorities. The university offers more than 60 bachelor's programmes and more than 200 master's programmes and specialisations. Its website lists faculties, including the Faculty of Humanities, the Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences and the Faculty of Law. Teaching is in Dutch and English.

university-of-birmingham.name: University of Birmingham
university-of-birmingham.brief: The University of Birmingham is a public research university in Birmingham, England. It received its royal charter in 1900 as a successor to Queen's College, Birmingham, and Mason Science College. It is the first English redbrick university to receive its own royal charter, and the first English unitary university. Its areas of study include accounting, medicine and health, engineering, law, business, and the sciences. Its academic structure includes colleges such as Arts and Law, Engineering and Physical Sciences, Life and Environmental Sciences, Medicine and Health, and Social Sciences, with schools and departments within them.

university-of-california-davis.name: University of California, Davis
university-of-california-davis.brief: The University of California, Davis is a public land-grant research university in Davis, California, United States. It is the northernmost of the ten campuses of the University of California system. The university is located in the central valley of Northern California. Its main areas of study include agriculture, biological sciences, engineering, and letters and science. Its academic structure includes four colleges and several schools, including the School of Law, School of Medicine, School of Nursing, School of Education, and School of Veterinary Medicine.

universitat-freiburg.brief: The University of Freiburg is a public research university in Freiburg im Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It was founded in 1457. Its areas of study include the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering and university medicine. The university has eleven faculties, among them Faculty of Biology, Faculty of Law and Faculty of Medicine. It has around 240 degree programmes.

university-of-leeds.brief: The University of Leeds is a public research university in Leeds, West Yorkshire, England. It was established in 1874 as the Yorkshire College of Science. Its main areas of study include arts, humanities and cultures, business, engineering and physical sciences, environment and social sciences, and health and life sciences. The university is divided into five faculties. Its campus map lists many named buildings across the city, including Clarendon Wing, Clothworkers' Building and Parkinson Building.

university-of-maryland-college-park.brief: The University of Maryland, College Park is a public land-grant research university in College Park, Maryland, United States. It is the flagship institution of the University System of Maryland. It offers over 100 undergraduate majors and more than 230 master's, doctoral and certificate programs. Its areas include agriculture and natural resources, architecture, arts and humanities, business, computer and natural sciences, education, engineering, information, journalism, public health and public policy. Academic units are organised as colleges and schools.

universite-de-montpellier.brief: The University of Montpellier is a public university in Montpellier, in the Occitanie region of southern France. The home page gives its founding as "The Future Since 1220". Its main fields are law, economics, management, political and social sciences, science, technology, and health. It is organised into 17 faculties, schools, and institutes, located in Montpellier and in cities in the eastern part of the Occitanie region, including Béziers, Nîmes and Sète. Its campuses include Richter and Triolet.

the-university-of-nottingham.name: University of Nottingham
the-university-of-nottingham.brief: The University of Nottingham is a public research university in Nottingham, England, founded as University College Nottingham in 1881 and granted a royal charter as a university in 1948. It has campuses in Nottingham and at Ningbo in China and in Malaysia. Its academic departments are grouped into faculties including Arts, Engineering, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science, and Social Sciences. Its main campuses in the UK include University Park, Jubilee and Sutton Bonington.

university-of-pennsylvania.name: University of Pennsylvania
university-of-pennsylvania.brief: University of Pennsylvania is a private research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. It was chartered in 1755 by its first president, Benjamin Franklin, and is one of nine colonial colleges in the country. Its areas of study include arts and sciences, engineering and applied science, nursing, business, communication, dental medicine, education, law, medicine, and social policy and practice. The university has 12 schools sharing one contiguous campus.

university-of-rochester.name: University of Rochester
university-of-rochester.brief: The University of Rochester is a private research university in Rochester, New York, United States. It was founded in 1850. Its main areas of study include humanities, health care, business, education, music, and engineering. The university offers 200+ undergraduate and graduate areas of study. Its schools include the School of Arts & Sciences, Hajim School of Engineering, Eastman School of Music, School of Medicine & Dentistry, School of Nursing & Health Sciences, Simon Business School, and Warner School of Education. Its main academic campus is the River Campus, next to the Genesee River.

university-of-southern-queensland.name: University of Southern Queensland
university-of-southern-queensland.brief: The University of Southern Queensland is a public research university based in Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia. It was founded in 1967 after a campaign by the local Darling Downs community. Its main areas of study include Arts and Communication, Aviation, Business, Education and Teaching, Engineering and Surveying, Health, Information Technology, Law, and Sciences and Agriculture. It has three distinct campuses: Toowoomba, Springfield and Ipswich, plus UniSQ Brisbane. Its academic structure is organised into five schools.

university-of-sussex.brief: The University of Sussex is a public research university in Falmer, East Sussex, England, lying mostly within the city boundaries of Brighton and Hove. It describes itself as research-intensive. Its research covers environmental sustainability, human flourishing, digital and data futures, and language. Visitors can join virtual Open Days and tours.

university-of-twente.name: University of Twente
university-of-twente.brief: The University of Twente is a public technical university located in Enschede, Netherlands. It works across engineering, social sciences and natural sciences, with study areas including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Health, Sustainability, Chip Technology and Design & Tech. The university's campus is in the Twente region, between the cities of Hengelo and Enschede, and it offers a Master's in Leeuwarden. Its main campus is Enschede, where the university is organised around its faculties and institutes.

university-of-waterloo.name: University of Waterloo
university-of-waterloo.brief: The University of Waterloo is a public research university in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. It opened in 1957, with engineering and co-operative education as cornerstones. Its main areas of study include engineering, arts, environment, health, mathematics and science. The university has six faculties, a main campus, and 3 satellite campuses, and it has affiliated and federated institutions.

universitat-erlangen-nurnberg.name: Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
universitat-erlangen-nurnberg.brief: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg is a public research university in Erlangen and Nuremberg in Bavaria, Germany. Founded in 1743, it offers 278 degree programs in five faculties, covering humanities, social sciences, theology, business, economics, law, medicine, sciences and engineering. Other FAU locations include Bayreuth, Bamberg, Pleinfeld and Schlungenhof at the Altmühlsee. The university is organised into five faculties, with Erlangen and Nuremberg as its main locations.

western-sydney-university.brief: Western Sydney University is a multi-campus public research university in the Greater Western region of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. It was formerly the University of Western Sydney. Its main areas of study include health, engineering, computing and science, social sciences, arts, business, education and law. It is organised into faculties, including the Faculty of Health, the Faculty of Engineering, Computing and Science, and the Faculty of Social Sciences, Arts, Business, Education and Law. Its campuses are spread across western Sydney, and it also has an international campus in Surabaya.

aix-marseille-university.name: Aix-Marseille University
aix-marseille-university.brief: Aix-Marseille University (Aix Marseille Université, amU) is a public research university in the Provence region of southern France. It was founded in 1409 as the University of Provence. Its areas of study include arts, humanities, languages, social sciences, law, political science, economics, management, science, technology, and health sciences such as medicine, pharmacy and dentistry. It is organised into five major campuses in Aix-en-Provence, Marseille, and other cities, and into faculties and schools.

australian-national-university.brief: The Australian National University (ANU) is a public research university in Canberra, the capital of Australia. It is a member of the Group of Eight. Its main campus is in Acton, Canberra. The university has six academic colleges covering areas such as arts and social sciences, Asia and the Pacific, business and economics, law, governance and policy, science and medicine, and systems and society. It also has campuses and facilities in the ACT, NSW and the NT, including Kioloa Coastal Campus and Siding Spring Observatory.

colorado-state-university.brief: Colorado State University is a public land-grant research university in Fort Collins, Colorado, United States. It is the flagship university of the Colorado State University System. The university offers nearly 300 academic programs, and over 70 majors, at undergraduate and graduate levels, and also through CSU Online. Its colleges include Agricultural Sciences, Business, Engineering, Health and Human Sciences, Liberal Arts, Natural Sciences, Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and Natural Resources.

dartmouth-college.name: Dartmouth College
dartmouth-college.brief: Dartmouth College is a private research university in Hanover, New Hampshire, United States. It was established in 1769 by Eleazar Wheelock and Samson Occom to train Native American Christian missionaries. Its main areas of study include over 40 departments and programs of the School of Arts and Sciences, plus graduate study in medicine, engineering, business and graduate studies. The university is organised into its School of Arts & Sciences, Geisel School of Medicine, Guarini School of Graduate & Advanced Studies, Thayer School of Engineering and Tuck School of Business. Its main campus covers 269 acres.

eberhard-karls-universitat-tubingen.name: Eberhard Karls Universität Tübingen
eberhard-karls-universitat-tubingen.brief: The University of Tübingen (Eberhard Karls Universität Tübingen) is a public research university in the city of Tübingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Its faculties include Protestant Theology, Catholic Theology, Law, Medicine, Humanities, Economics and Social Sciences, and Science, plus a Center for Islamic Theology. The university's "Life on campus" section and its maps and "How to get here" pages are part of its website.

freie-universitat-berlin.name: Freie Universität Berlin
freie-universitat-berlin.brief: Freie Universität Berlin is a public research university in Berlin, Germany. It was founded in West Berlin in 1948 during the early Cold War period. The university says it has stood for truth, justice, and freedom since its founding in 1948. Its research and teaching have an international focus, and people from more than 150 countries work and study there. Its Student Service Center is on Iltisstraße, next to the Dahlem Dorf subway station (U3).

universite-grenoble-alpes.name: Grenoble Alpes University
universite-grenoble-alpes.brief: Université Grenoble Alpes is a grand établissement in Grenoble, France. The university works in research, teaching and innovation across the Alps region and the Domaine universitaire at Saint-Martin-d'Hères. Its academic components include the École nationale supérieure d'architecture de Grenoble, Grenoble INP and Sciences Po Grenoble. It also works with national research organisations.

indiana-university-bloomington.brief: Indiana University Bloomington is a public research university in Bloomington, Indiana, United States. It is the flagship campus of Indiana University. Main areas of study include art, design and performance; business and organizations; communication; education; science, technology and engineering; health and wellness; environment; society, community and culture; global perspectives; and law and justice. Its academic units are organised as schools and colleges.

The university has schools including the School of Architecture + Planning, the School of Engineering, the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences, the Sloan School of Management, the School of Science, and the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing. murdoch-university.brief: Murdoch University is a public university in Perth, Western Australia, with additional campuses in Singapore and Dubai. northeastern-university.brief: Northeastern University is a private research university in the United States, with its main campus in Boston, Massachusetts. It was founded by the Boston Young Men's Christian Association in 1898 and gained university status in 1922. Main areas of study include health sciences, arts, media and design, engineering, business, computer sciences, law, science and social sciences and humanities. It was established in 2019 after the merger of four technical grandes écoles, as well as several technological institutes, engineering schools, and research facilities. It covers science and engineering, life sciences and health, and humanities and social sciences. Its education follows the European LMD scheme. It is organised into constituent colleges, including faculties, technical institutes, engineering schools and grandes écoles.

queen-s-university-ontario.name: Queen's University
queen-s-university-ontario.brief: Queen's University is a public research university in Kingston, Ontario, Canada. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs and postdoctoral fellowships, with more than 235 academic areas across 53 departments. Its main areas include arts and science, education, health sciences, law, business and engineering. Its faculties and schools are the Faculty of Arts and Science, Faculty of Education, School of Graduate Studies and Postdoctoral Affairs, Faculty of Health Sciences, Faculty of Law, Smith Business and Smith Engineering. The university also holds land across Ontario and owns Herstmonceux Castle in East Sussex, England.

rice-university.name: Rice University
rice-university.brief: Rice University is a private research university in Houston, Texas, United States. Its main areas of study include engineering and computing, business, architecture, humanities and arts, social sciences, music, and natural sciences. It is organised into schools, including the George R. Brown School of Engineering and Computing, the Jesse H. Jones Graduate School of Business, and the Wiess School of Natural Sciences. stony-brook-university.name: Stony Brook University
stony-brook-university.brief: Stony Brook University is a public research university in Stony Brook, New York, on Long Island, United States. It is one of the two flagship institutions of the State University of New York system, along with the University at Buffalo. The university offers undergraduate and graduate study across its colleges and schools, including the College of Arts and Sciences and the College of Business. Its campuses include Stony Brook and Stony Brook Southampton.

technische-universitat-bergakademie-frei.name: Technische Universität Bergakademie Freiberg
technische-universitat-bergakademie-frei.brief: Technische Universität Bergakademie Freiberg is a public university of technology in Freiberg, Saxony, Germany. Its focuses are exploration, mining and extraction, processing, and recycling of natural resources and scrap, as well as developing new materials and researching renewable energies. Faculties include Mathematics and Computer Science, Chemistry, Physics and Bioscience, Geosciences, Geoengineering and Mining, Mechanical, Process and Energy Engineering, Materials Science and Technology, and Business Administration.

trinity-college-dublin-the-university-of.brief: Trinity College Dublin is a university in Dublin, Ireland, and the sole constituent college of the University of Dublin. It was founded in 1592 by Queen Elizabeth I through a royal charter. Its main areas of study are arranged in three faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Health Sciences; and Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics. The university has 3 campuses and 13 schools and colleges. Its schools include Architecture and Planning, Arts and Sciences, Engineering and Applied Sciences, Law, Management, Nursing, and Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences. university-of-arizona.brief: The University of Arizona is a public land-grant research university in Tucson, Arizona, United States. It was founded in 1885 by the 13th Arizona Territorial Legislature. Main areas of study include agriculture, architecture, education, engineering, fine arts, humanities, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, public health, science, and veterinary medicine. It has 20 colleges and schools, and more than 150 majors and programs of study.

universite-de-bordeaux.name: University of Bordeaux
universite-de-bordeaux.brief: The University of Bordeaux is a public research university in Nouvelle-Aquitaine, southwestern France. Its main areas of study include biological and medical sciences, public health, health sciences and technologies, environmental sciences, engineering and digital sciences, material and light sciences, social sciences, law and archaeological sciences. The university has campuses in Agen, Bordeaux (La Bastide, Carreire, Montesquieu, Peixotto and Bordes, Victoire), Dax, Périgord and Rocquencourt, plus several sites.

university-of-california-irvine.name: University of California, Irvine
university-of-california-irvine.brief: University of California, Irvine is a public land-grant research university in Irvine, California, United States. It is one of the ten campuses of the University of California system. The university offers programmes across 15 schools, including biological sciences, arts, information and computer sciences, engineering, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, business, education, humanities, physical sciences, social ecology, social sciences and population and public health. Pitt offers over 100 degree programs at the Pittsburgh campus and more than 40 majors, minors, concentrations and pre-professional programs at its Bradford campus. Its colleges and schools include Arts & Sciences, Business, Engineering, Medicine, Nursing and Law. Regional campuses are in Bradford, Greensburg, Johnstown and Titusville.

university-of-saskatchewan.name: University of Saskatchewan
university-of-saskatchewan.brief: The University of Saskatchewan is a Canadian public research university located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada, on the east side of the South Saskatchewan River. It was founded on March 19, 1907. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs in over 200 fields of study, including statistics, engineering, agriculture, medicine, law and nursing. Its academic structure includes colleges and schools such as Arts and Science, Engineering, Medicine and Edwards School of Business, along with federated and affiliated colleges. Founded in 1413, it is Scotland's oldest university and the third oldest in the English-speaking world. Its main areas of study include Art History, Biology, Chemistry, Classics, Computer Science, Divinity, English, History, International Relations, Mathematics and Statistics, Medicine, Physics and Psychology. The university is organised into Academic Schools, Institutes and Centres, and its Schools are grouped into four Faculties. It has more than 120 countries represented in its student population.

Its areas of study include architecture, design and planning, arts and social sciences, business, economics, education and social work, engineering, computer science and project management, law, medicine and health, music, and science. It offers more than 280 undergraduate and graduate programs in areas including business, education, engineering and computer science, fine arts, health, humanities, law, science, and social sciences. Its campus is at 3800 Finnerty Road, Victoria, BC. Faculties and schools include Business, Education, Engineering and Computer Science, Fine Arts, Graduate Studies, Health, Humanities, Law, Science, and Social Sciences, along with the Division of Continuing Studies.

the-university-of-western-australia.name: University of Western Australia
the-university-of-western-australia.brief: The University of Western Australia (UWA) is a public research university in Crawley, Western Australia, Australia. It was established in 1911 by an act of the Parliament of Western Australia. Its main areas of study include arts, science, business, health, law, engineering, education and music. It is organised into schools, with campuses in Perth and Albany.

laval-university.name: Laval University
laval-university.brief: Université Laval is a public research university in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada. Its roots go back to the Séminaire de Québec, founded by François de Montmorency-Laval in 1663. The university offers programs in areas such as agriculture and food sciences, arts and humanities, business administration, dental medicine, education, forestry, geography and geomatics, law, music, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, philosophy, planning, architecture, art and design, science and engineering, social sciences, and theology and religious sciences. loughborough-university.name: Loughborough University
loughborough-university.brief: Loughborough University is a public research university in the market town of Loughborough, Leicestershire, England. It has been a university since 1966, and it dates back to 1909, when Loughborough Technical Institute was founded. Its areas of study include engineering, sport, business, science, social sciences and humanities, and creative arts.

massey-university.brief: Massey University is a public research university in New Zealand that provides internal and distance education. It offers 170 qualifications and over 2,700 courses, with postgraduate study among its options. Its main campuses are in Auckland, Palmerston North (Manawatū), and Wellington, plus a Singapore campus. The university has four colleges: Massey Business School, College of Creative Arts, College of Health, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and College of Sciences.

It was founded in 1981 and is the second oldest autonomous university in the country. Its main areas of study include engineering, computing and data science, business, humanities, arts and social sciences, science, and medicine, plus education through the National Institute of Education. The university is organised into colleges and schools, including the College of Engineering, College of Science and College of Business (Nanyang Business School). Its address is 50 Nanyang Avenue, Singapore 639798.

technische-universitat-berlin.brief: Technische Universität Berlin is a public research university located in Berlin, Germany. Its main areas of study include humanities and educational sciences, mathematics and natural sciences, process sciences, electrical engineering and computer science, mechanical engineering and transport systems, planning and building environment, and economics and management. tufts-university.brief: Tufts University is a private research university in Medford and Somerville, Massachusetts, United States, with additional facilities in Boston and Grafton, as well as Talloires, France. It was founded in 1852 as Tufts College by Christian universalists who sought to provide a nonsectarian institution of higher learning. It brings together undergraduate, graduate, professional, and lifelong learning across 10 schools and colleges. Areas of study include arts and sciences, biomedical sciences, veterinary medicine, dental medicine, engineering, diplomacy, nutrition, and medicine.

universiti-malaya.brief: Universiti Malaya is a public research university in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It is the oldest Malaysian institution of higher education. Its academic programmes cover a broad spectrum of knowledge, with study offered at undergraduate and postgraduate level in coursework, mixed-mode, research and clinical tracks. The university is organised into faculties, including Medicine, Engineering, Law, Business and Economics, and Computer Science and Information Technology.

university-college-cork.name: University College Cork
university-college-cork.brief: University College Cork (UCC) is a constituent university of the National University of Ireland, located in Cork, Ireland. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate, international, adult continuing education and microcredential study options. Its schools and departments cover areas including medicine and health, business and law, science, engineering and food science, arts, celtic studies and social sciences, and education.

It was established as Auckland University College, a constituent college of the University of New Zealand, and formally opened in 1883. Its main areas of study include Arts and Education, Business, Engineering and Design, Law, Medical and Health Sciences, and Science.

university-of-bristol.name: University of Bristol
university-of-bristol.brief: The University of Bristol is a public research university in Bristol, England. It received its royal charter in 1909, and can trace its roots to University College, Bristol, established in 1876. Its main areas of study are arranged in three faculties: Arts, Law and Social Sciences; Health and Life Sciences; and Science and Engineering. It also has a campus in Mumbai, the University of Bristol Mumbai Enterprise Campus, which offers three-year undergraduate and one-year postgraduate programmes.

university-of-california-los-angeles.name: University of California, Los Angeles
university-of-california-los-angeles.brief: The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is a public land-grant research university in the Westwood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, United States. Its academic roots were established in 1881 as the southern branch of the California State Normal School. UCLA offers degrees across the College and professional schools, including the arts, architecture, dentistry, education, engineering, law, management, medicine, music, nursing and public affairs. It has 13 faculties and schools, including Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal.

vrije-universiteit-amsterdam.name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
vrije-universiteit-amsterdam.brief: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is a public research university in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It was founded in 1880. It offers bachelor's and master's programmes, a PhD, honours programmes, summer school and Dutch language courses. Its pages mention research institutes and Faculties; the home page lists Faculties and Divisions as separate sections.

york-university.name: York University
york-university.brief: York University is a public research university based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. It is Canada's third-largest university. Its main areas of study include arts, education, environmental and urban change, health, engineering, liberal arts and professional studies, law, business, and science. York has three core campuses in the Toronto area: Keele, Glendon and Markham. Its Faculties include the School of the Arts, Media, Performance & Design, Lassonde School of Engineering and Osgoode Hall Law School.

american-university-of-sharjah.name: American University of Sharjah
american-university-of-sharjah.brief: The American University of Sharjah is a private university in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. It was founded in 1997 by Sultan bin Muhammad Al-Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah. It offers 33 undergraduate majors, 24 master's degree programs and eight PhD programs. Its academic units are the College of Architecture, Art and Design, College of Arts and Sciences, College of Engineering and School of Business Administration.

boston-university.name: Boston University
boston-university.brief: Boston University is a private research university in Boston, Massachusetts, United States. It was founded in 1839 by a group of Boston Methodists, with its original campus in Newbury, Vermont. The university offers programmes across its schools and colleges, including a Medical Campus. Its Charles River Campus is referred to by name on the faculty pages. The university has more than 130 research centers and institutes.

case-western-reserve-university.name: Case Western Reserve University
case-western-reserve-university.brief: Case Western Reserve University is a private research university in Cleveland, Ohio, United States. It was federated in 1967 by a merger between Western Reserve University, founded in 1826 by the Presbyterian Church, and the Case Institute of Technology, founded in 1880. Its programmes include undergraduate, graduate and professional, and online programmes. Its schools include the School of Medicine and the Case School of Engineering. Its campus is in University Circle.

concordia-university.name: Concordia University
concordia-university.brief: Concordia University is a public English-language research university in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It was founded in 1974 through the merger of Loyola College and Sir George Williams University. Its main areas of study include Arts and Science, Fine Arts, Engineering and Computer Science, Business, Graduate Studies and Health. The university has two campuses in Montreal, the Sir George Williams Campus downtown and the Loyola Campus.

delft-university-of-technology.name: Delft University of Technology
delft-university-of-technology.brief: Delft University of Technology is a public technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. It specialises in engineering, technology, computing, design, and natural sciences. The university has eight faculties, which accommodate almost 40 technological and scientific disciplines. Research institutes include QuTech and the TU Delft Reactor Institute. Its campus is in Delft, with a campus map and tours available.

faculties.name: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

eindhoven-university-of-technology.name: Eindhoven University of Technology
eindhoven-university-of-technology.brief: Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) is a public technical university in Eindhoven, the Netherlands. The university was founded in 1956 at the request of the region's high-tech industry. It has nine departments, including Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science, Built Environment, and Industrial Design. Its main campus, TU/e Campus, is located near the train station and city centre of Eindhoven. The university works closely with industry in the Brainport Eindhoven region.

george-washington-university.name: George Washington University
george-washington-university.brief: The George Washington University is a private federally chartered research university in Washington, D.C., United States. It was chartered in 1821 by the United States Congress as the Columbian College. Its schools and colleges include the Columbian College of Arts & Sciences, Corcoran School of the Arts & Design, School of Business, Graduate School of Education & Human Development, and School of Engineering & Applied Science. The university has campuses at Foggy Bottom, Mount Vernon, and the Virginia Science & Technology Campus, plus online and Virginia academic centers.

harvard-university.name: Harvard University
harvard-university.brief: Harvard University is a private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States. It was founded in 1636 and is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States. Its main areas of study include undergraduate and graduate degrees, professional schools, and fields such as neurobiology, engineering and applied sciences, medicine, and public health. The university's three main campuses are in Cambridge, Allston, and Boston. It consists of the undergraduate Harvard College, 12 graduate and professional Schools, and the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study.

institut-polytechnique-de-paris.name: Institut Polytechnique de Paris
institut-polytechnique-de-paris.brief: Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris) is a public institution for higher education and research in Palaiseau, France. It brings together six engineering schools: École polytechnique, ENSTA Paris, École nationale des ponts et chaussées, ENSAE Paris, Télécom Paris and Télécom SudParis. Main areas include artificial intelligence and data science, mathematics, quantum technologies, cybersecurity, energy transition and economics. Education is offered at bachelor, engineering, master and PhD levels. The Institute's campus has ecosystem, infrastructure, libraries and student life facilities.

justus-liebig-universitat-gieen.name: Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen
justus-liebig-universitat-gieen.brief: Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen is a large public research university in Giessen, Hesse, Germany. It is one of the oldest institutions of higher education in the German-speaking world. The university was founded in 1607. It describes itself as a comprehensive university, with study areas from Accounting, Finance & Sustainability to Dentistry. Its organisation includes eleven faculties (Faculty 01 to Faculty 11), plus research centres and a university-wide service facility structure.

leibniz-universitat-hannover.name: Leibniz University Hannover
leibniz-universitat-hannover.brief: Leibniz University Hannover is a public research university in Hanover, Germany. It was founded on 2 May 1831 as Higher Vocational School. Its main subject areas include Engineering and Technology, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Law and Economics, Humanities and Social Sciences, and Linguistics and Literature. The university has nine faculties, including Architecture and Landscape Sciences, Civil Engineering and Geodetic Science, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, and Mechanical Engineering. Its campuses include Welfengarten, Conti-Campus (Königsworther Platz), Schneiderberg, Herrenhausen and Maschinenbau Garbsen.

ludwig-maximilians-universitat-munchen.name: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
ludwig-maximilians-universitat-munchen.brief: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München is a public research university in Munich, Bavaria, Germany. It was originally established as the University of Ingolstadt in 1472. Its areas of study include humanities, culture, law, economics, business, social sciences, physics, medicine, mathematics, informatics, statistics, natural and life sciences, and veterinary medicine. It has five campus sites: Geschwister-Scholl-Platz, English Garden, Sendlinger Tor, Grosshadern / Martinsried and Oberschleissheim.

mcgill-university.name: McGill University
mcgill-university.brief: McGill University is an English-language public research university in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It was founded in 1821 by royal charter and bears the name of James McGill. Its faculties include Engineering, Law, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science, and Management. Its main campuses include the downtown campus and the Macdonald campus. The university is organised into faculties and schools, including the Faculty of Arts and the Schulich School of Music.

national-university-of-singapore.name: National University of Singapore
national-university-of-singapore.brief: The National University of Singapore (NUS) is a national public research university in Singapore. It was officially established in 1980 through the merger of the University of Singapore and Nanyang University. The university has departments in areas including accounting, architecture, biomedical engineering, computer science, law, medicine, and pharmacy. Its faculties and schools include Arts & Social Sciences, Dentistry, Law, Medicine, and Science. Its address is 21 Lower Kent Ridge Road, Singapore 119077.

norwegian-university-of-science-and-tech.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
norwegian-university-of-science-and-tech.brief: NTNU (Norges teknisk-naturvitenskapelige universitet) is a public research university in Norway. Its headquarters is in Trondheim, with campuses in Gjøvik and Ålesund. The university's areas of study include architecture and design, humanities, information technology and electrical engineering, engineering, medicine and health sciences, natural sciences, social sciences and education, economics, and museum studies. It is organised into faculties, each with institutes.

royal-holloway-university-of-london.brief: Royal Holloway, University of London is a public research university and a member institution of the federal University of London. It is located in Egham, Surrey, with a Central London campus in Bloomsbury. It was founded in 1849 as Bedford College, and the two colleges merged in 1985 to form the present university. Its main areas of study include business and management and law. It has 3 faculties and 12 academic departments.

simon-fraser-university.name: Simon Fraser University
simon-fraser-university.brief: Simon Fraser University is a public research university in British Columbia, Canada. It has three campuses in Greater Vancouver: Burnaby, Surrey and Vancouver. Its campuses are in B.C.'s three largest cities. The university has faculties and departments, and it has a Research section with institutes and centres.

swansea-university.name: Swansea University
swansea-university.brief: Swansea University is a public research university in Swansea, Wales. It was established as University College of Swansea in 1920, as the fourth college of the University of Wales. Its faculties cover humanities and social sciences, medicine, health and life science, and science and engineering. The university has two campuses, Singleton Campus and Bay Campus, both on the coast. Its faculties are set along the stunning south-west Wales coast.

technische-universitat-darmstadt.name: Technische Universität Darmstadt
technische-universitat-darmstadt.brief: Technische Universität Darmstadt (TU Darmstadt) is a public research university in the city of Darmstadt, Germany. It was founded in 1877 and received the right to award doctorates in 1899. Its focus is engineering and natural sciences, closely linked with humanities and social sciences. Subject areas include architecture, civil and environmental engineering, electrical engineering and information technology, computer science, mechanical engineering, biology, chemistry, mathematics, physics, and law and economics. Campuses include Stadtmitte and Lichtwiese.

ucl.name: UCL (University College London)
ucl.brief: University College London (UCL) is a public research university in London, England. It was founded in 1826 as London's very first university. It is a member institution of the federal University of London. UCL has 11 faculties, covering areas such as arts and humanities, medicine, law, engineering, mathematical and physical sciences, and social and historical sciences. Its main address is Gower Street, London.

university-of-bath.name: University of Bath
university-of-bath.brief: The University of Bath is a public research university in Bath, England. It was established on Claverton Down in Bath in 1966. It is a campus university in the South West of England. The university offers courses in engineering, humanities, management, science and social science. Its main campus is at Claverton Down, and its academic structure includes faculties and the School of Management.

university-of-british-columbia.name: University of British Columbia
university-of-british-columbia.brief: The University of British Columbia (UBC) is a public research university in British Columbia, Canada. Its two main campuses are near Vancouver and in Kelowna, in the Okanagan region. Its main areas of study include research across many fields, with a Faculty of Medicine across BC. Its two major campuses are in Vancouver and the Okanagan, and it also has UBC Robson Square and the Centre for Digital Media.

university-of-california-riverside.name: University of California, Riverside
university-of-california-riverside.brief: The University of California, Riverside is a public land-grant research university in Riverside, California, United States, and one of the ten campuses of the University of California system. The university has been accredited since 1956. Its campus covers 1200 acres, and it has a Botany and Plant Sciences Department. The university is organised into campuses and faculties.

university-of-canterbury.name: University of Canterbury
university-of-canterbury.brief: The University of Canterbury is a public research university in Christchurch, New Zealand. It was founded in 1873 as Canterbury College, the first constituent college of the University of New Zealand. Its main area of study includes Arts, Business, Education and Teaching, Engineering, Health, Law and Criminal Justice, and Science. The main campus is Ilam in Christchurch, with other locations including Dovedale campus, Arts Centre, Nelson campus, and field stations.

university-of-gothenburg.name: University of Gothenburg
university-of-gothenburg.brief: The University of Gothenburg is a public university in Gothenburg, Sweden. It was founded in 1891. Its main areas of study include sustainability and the environment, health and medicine, culture and languages, science and IT, society and economics, and education and learning. The university is one of Sweden's largest educational institutions. Its campus is the whole city, and it has 7 faculties.

university-of-kent.name: University of Kent
university-of-kent.brief: The University of Kent is a university in Kent, England, and part of the London and South East University Group (LASE). It was an independent university from 1965, when it was founded by royal charter, until 2026, when it merged with the University of Greenwich to form LASE. Its campuses are in Canterbury and Medway. Its Schools and Colleges team works with local schools and colleges, and it offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses. The university also has a business services unit that works with employers and public bodies.

university-of-liverpool.name: University of Liverpool
university-of-liverpool.brief: The University of Liverpool is a public research university in Liverpool, England, in the United Kingdom. It was founded in 1881 as University College Liverpool. Its main areas include health and life sciences, humanities and social sciences, and science and engineering. Its teaching is organised into 3 specialist Faculties, which contain schools and departments. The university also has a campus in Bengaluru, India, and a campus shown as China in the site's campus selector.

university-of-miami.name: University of Miami
university-of-miami.brief: The University of Miami is a private research university in Coral Gables, Florida, United States. It offers more than 180 academic programs and majors across its Schools and Colleges. The university has 12 Schools and Colleges on three campuses in Coral Gables, Virginia Key, and downtown Miami. The Coral Gables campus is its main campus, home to two colleges and seven schools. The Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine campus is in the Health District near downtown Miami, and the Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science is on Virginia Key.

university-of-ottawa.name: University of Ottawa
university-of-ottawa.brief: The University of Ottawa is a bilingual public research university in Ottawa, Ontario, the capital city of Canada. Teaching is in English and French. Its main campus is located on 42.5 hectares in the Sandy Hill neighbourhood, northeast of Downtown Ottawa across the Rideau Canal. It was founded in 1848 (the site says "Since 1848"). Its main areas of study are arts, education, engineering, health sciences, law, medicine, science, social sciences and management.

universiti-putra-malaysia.name: University of Putra Malaysia
universiti-putra-malaysia.brief: Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) is a public research university in Serdang, Selangor, Malaysia. It was formerly named Universiti Pertanian Malaysia and focuses on agricultural sciences and related fields. The university's homepage highlights work in agriculture, forestry, veterinary sciences, food security and community well-being.

the-university-of-sheffield.name: University of Sheffield
the-university-of-sheffield.brief: The University of Sheffield is a public research university in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England. It traces its history to Sheffield Medical School (founded in 1828), Firth College (1879) and Sheffield Technical School (1884), which came together in 1897 as the University College of Sheffield and became the University of Sheffield in 1905. university-of-strathclyde.name: University of Strathclyde
university-of-strathclyde.brief: The University of Strathclyde is a public research university in Glasgow, Scotland. It was founded as the Andersonian Institute in 1796 and received its royal charter in 1964. Its main areas of study include engineering, humanities and social sciences, science, and business. The university is organised into faculties and departments, including the Faculty of Engineering, the Faculty of Humanities & Social Sciences, the Faculty of Science, and the Strathclyde Business School. Its campus is in Glasgow city centre.

university-of-technology-sydney.name: University of Technology Sydney
university-of-technology-sydney.brief: University of Technology Sydney (UTS) is a public research university in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. The university was founded in its current form in 1988, and its origins as a technical institution can be traced back to the 1870s. Its areas of study include business, design, engineering and IT, health, law, science and social sciences. Its main campus is the City Campus at 15 Broadway, Ultimo, NSW 2007. Its faculties include the UTS Business School, the Faculty of Design and Society, the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, the Faculty of Health, the Faculty of Law and the Faculty of Science.

university-of-waikato.name: University of Waikato
university-of-waikato.brief: The University of Waikato is a public research university in Hamilton, New Zealand. It also has a campus in Tauranga. It was established in 1964. Its pages mention study areas including business, engineering, nursing, medicine, arts, law, and science. The Hamilton campus is in the Hillcrest suburb. university-of-wisconsin-madison.name: University of Wisconsin–Madison
university-of-wisconsin-madison.brief: The University of Wisconsin–Madison is a public land-grant research university in Madison, Wisconsin, United States. It was founded in 1848 when Wisconsin achieved statehood and is the flagship campus of the University of Wisconsin System. The university describes its work across the humanities and the hard sciences, and its research enterprise is one of the 10 largest in the country. It has a lakeside campus, and its schools and colleges prepare students for careers after graduation.
